payload.verdict: A customer success manager with a defined SaaS portfolio, but few details about renewals and what changed.
write_up: Your resume tells a consistent customer-facing story, from account coordination at Brightpath Logistics to customer success at Northwind Analytics. A recruiter could move it forward for a Customer Success Manager role, with questions about what your renewal work involved and what came from it.

The strongest line names 32 B2B SaaS accounts and $2.4M in annual recurring revenue. It gives a recruiter a concrete picture of your portfolio. The objective above your experience is much more generic and doesn't point to that work.

Let's start by replacing the objective with your customer success work, then fill in your part in renewals and the risk reviews. You don't need a number on every line: the quarterly business reviews and weekly shipment reports already name work a recruiter can follow.

cards.line: Results-driven, detail-oriented professional seeking a challenging role where I can utilize my skills.
cards.cannot_tell: This could describe almost anyone, and it doesn't name the customer success work below it. Lead with your portfolio instead.
cards.example: Customer Success Manager managing 32 B2B SaaS accounts with $2.4M in annual recurring revenue, seeking [target role]
cards.question: What role are you targeting?

cards.line: Responsible for managing customer relationships and renewals
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the portfolio on the next line, but not what you did to manage renewals. Did you coordinate the process, negotiate terms, or handle another part?
cards.example: Managed customer relationships and renewals by [renewal responsibilities]
cards.question: What parts of the renewal process did you handle?

cards.line: Managed 32 B2B SaaS accounts with $2.4M in annual recurring revenue
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It pairs your ownership with the kind of accounts and their revenue, so a recruiter doesn't have to guess what you managed.

cards.line: Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews across the portfolio
cards.cannot_tell: Introducing the reviews is useful work. What the reviews covered and what followed them would show why they mattered.
cards.example: Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews across the portfolio, covering [review topics] and [follow-up actions]
cards.question: What did the reviews cover, and what actions followed them?

cards.line: Team player with excellent communication skills
cards.cannot_tell: This tells a recruiter how you describe yourself, not what you did. Replace it with a customer or team interaction that shows those skills in use.
cards.example: Worked with [people or teams] on [customer success work]
cards.question: What customer or team work could you describe here?

cards.line: Assisted account managers with various tasks as needed
cards.cannot_tell: Assisted keeps your role honest, but various tasks leaves the work blank. Name the tasks you handled for the account managers.
cards.example: Assisted account managers with [account management tasks]
cards.question: Which tasks did you handle for the account managers?

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell which Office applications you used, and the two broad skills don't show where you used them. Name the applications and other job-related skills you can back up.
cards.example: Microsoft Office: [applications used]; [other customer success skills]
cards.question: Which Office applications and customer success skills have you used in your work?

fit.why: Your current Customer Success Manager role covers a B2B SaaS portfolio, renewals, risk reviews and customer business reviews.
fit.level: Customer Success Manager, manages 32 B2B SaaS accounts
fit.note: Your experience points most directly toward customer success and account management work. Details about your renewal responsibilities and what followed the risk reviews would help distinguish your work within those roles.
